Under 40 years of age
Graduate degree
At least 3 years of ground-level work in the development sector

Not already a founder or co-founder of any registered organisation
Willing to relocate to and commit long-term to one of the four focus geographies

Monthly honorarium of ₹45,000 during the 8-month seeding phase (from 1 April 2027)
One-month residential boot camp and supported fieldwork
Hands-on help with registration, governance, compliance, finance, HR and programme design
Pathway to a two-year grant of ₹15–20 lakh per year for those who meet milestones

items.about: D-Prize gives first-time social entrepreneurs seed money to launch a venture that delivers an already-proven poverty intervention — such as ORS for childhood diarrhoea, reading glasses, water filters or post-harvest support — to people who still lack it. You pick one of its listed challenges (or propose your own) and pitch a distribution model you can pilot quickly. Regular round closes 15 Nov 2026 at midnight Pacific Time (about 1:30 PM IST on 16 Nov). A final extension deadline of 6 Dec 2026 is available only if you register for it on D-Prize's extension page. Round 1 needs a two-page concept note plus resumes; the top ~5% get two weeks to answer written questions, then interviews. Only around the top 1% of applicants are funded.
items.eligibility:
New ventures only: typically under 18 months of full-time operation and under US$30,000 raised
Existing organisations considered only if their core work is distributing an evidence-based poverty intervention
Must target one of D-Prize's challenge areas or a well-argued 'propose your own' intervention
Founders from low- and middle-income countries such as India are especially encouraged
Willing to run a pilot and then raise follow-on funding to scale
items.benefits:
Up to US$20,000 to launch and pilot the venture
Ongoing guidance from the D-Prize team during the pilot
Credibility with follow-on funders after a successful pilot
Light first round — only a two-page concept note and CVs

items.shortDesc: The second call of the ₹5,000 crore Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech (PRIP) scheme funds startups, MSMEs and industry building new drugs, biosimilars and novel medical devices. Early-stage projects start with a short concept note; later-stage projects apply directly with a detailed proposal.
items.fundingAmount: Up to ₹5 Cr (early stage) / ₹100 Cr (later stage)
items.provider: Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers
items.about: The second call of the ₹5,000 crore Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech (PRIP) scheme funds startups, MSMEs and industry building new drugs, biosimilars and novel medical devices. Early-stage projects start with a short concept note; later-stage projects apply directly with a detailed proposal. Submission window opened on the PRIP portal from mid-September 2026; no closing date has been announced, so apply early and check the portal. Later-stage awards need the applicant to co-fund at least 65% of the project. Novel device categories include AI/ML devices and SaMD/SiMD, genetic diagnostics, surgical robotics, telemedicine-enabled devices and novel IVDs/biomarkers.
items.eligibility:
Early-stage track: startups and MSMEs taking a product from TRL 1–3 up to (not beyond) TRL 5
Later-stage track: industry, startups and MSMEs taking a product from TRL 4–6 to higher readiness
Project must fall in a priority area: new chemical/biological entities, phyto-pharmaceuticals, complex generics, biosimilars, or novel medical devices not yet approved by CDSCO
Projects already submitted in PRIP Round 1 should not be resubmitted
Ecosystem enablers (incubators etc.) may submit early-stage concept notes on behalf of startups in their network
items.benefits:
Up to ₹5 crore per early-stage project
Up to ₹100 crore per later-stage project, covering up to 35% of approved project cost
Mentorship for commercialisation, plus MedTech Mitra and Patent Mitra support
Access to a collaboration platform linking industry, academia and startups
